problem: VLN agents trained on the few Matterport3D training scenes overfit to seen environments and drop sharply in unseen houses. Prior environment-level augmentation has gaps: EnvDrop's feature dropout is uninterpretable, and REM's environment mixing only recombines existing seen scenes, sometimes into unrealistic ones. Pre-training on web or AirBnB image-text data suffers a domain shift from VLN panoramas and human-written instructions.
motivation: Unseen environments differ from seen ones mainly in style, object appearance and furniture or object sets. Synthetic 'new' environments that keep the original semantics let the original human-written instructions be reused unchanged, which avoids low-quality speaker-generated instructions. This could give the agent visual diversity cheaply and interpretably, and it can be combined with both non-pretrained and pretrained VLN agents.
key_idea: Build new training environments by editing the existing Matterport3D panoramas in three ways while keeping their semantics: artistic style transfer, SPADE semantic image synthesis that changes object appearance, and SPADE with a randomly masked semantic class that changes objects. The agent is trained on half-original, half-edited batches with the original instructions, then fine-tuned with back-translation from a style-aware speaker.
insight: Environment-level augmentation helps only while it keeps a balance between instruction fidelity and visual diversity, and several ablations show this. (1) Sampling one style per viewpoint, shared by all 36 views of a panorama, is essential. Varying style inside a panorama drops SR by 2.3 (58.2→55.9, ViT-B/16), and fixing one style for the whole house drops SR by 2.4 (58.2→55.8). (2) Keeping the original style while changing appearance (E_is1) beats changing both (E_is2) by 2.0 SR with ViT-B/32. (3) Masking more semantic classes monotonically hurts: 57.3→55.6→54.6→54.2 SR for 1→4 masked classes. Different edits help different unseen scenes (e.g. scene 11: 16.7→55.6 SR with E_is1^m, but only 33.3 with E_st), so the edit types are complementary and ensembling them gains further. In contrast, sequential curriculum over original and edited environments (original-then-edited or edited-then-original, including multi-environment variants) underperforms simple mixed batches.
method: Style transfer E_st: the off-the-shelf style-augmentation network of Jackson et al. 2019 with conditional instance normalization. Style embeddings are sampled from a multivariate Gaussian fit to Painter-By-Numbers style embeddings. The same style is used for all 36 discretized views of a panorama, with a new style per viewpoint.

Semantic image synthesis E_is1 / E_is2: a SPADE GAN (hinge + feature-matching loss, KL-regularized style encoder) is trained for 10 epochs on R2R training environments and regenerates each view from its semantic segmentation. E_is1 uses the original view as the style image, so it keeps the style and changes appearance. E_is2 uses a fixed, e.g. all-zero, style embedding, so it changes both style and appearance.

Object editing E_is1^m / E_is2^m: an extra C+1 'mask' class is added. During SPADE training a random class is replaced by 'mask', and at editing time one random class is masked, which removes or changes objects (e.g. a cabinet or pictures). E_is1^m keeps the style and E_is2^m changes style, appearance and objects.

Mixed training: in each batch of N instruction-path pairs, half see original and half see edited features (CLIP ViT-B/16 or B/32 re-extracted on the edited images). The original human instructions are reused, and training uses IL+RL as in EnvDrop. The same scheme fine-tunes pretrained HAMT and RecBERT.

Style-aware speaker for back-translation: the EnvDrop speaker's LSTM decoder is initialized from an FC-projected style embedding. This embedding is the mean of the StyleEncoder output over the 36 views at the start viewpoint. The speaker generates instructions for unannotated paths, and the agent is fine-tuned on original plus synthetic pairs.
Ensemble: agents trained on E_st, E_is1 and E_is1^m are combined by averaging their action logits at test time; this is used for the leaderboard HAMT submissions.

setting.backbone: EnvDrop-CLIP (LSTM seq2seq agent trained from scratch; multilingual BERT-base instruction encoder on RxR) or HAMT (pre-trained transformer, fine-tuned), both on frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 or ViT-B/32 image features; also RecBERT in the appendix
setting.training_data: R2R / RxR training splits, augmented with 5 kinds of edited copies of the 61 training scenes. Style transfer uses PBN painting-style statistics; SPADE is trained on R2R training scenes. Back-translation uses speaker-generated instructions for unannotated training-scene paths (EnvDrop protocol). HAMT and RecBERT start from their released pretrained weights.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views, CLIP features + heading/elevation orientation features)

numbers_note: All numbers come from tables. The RxR test paragraph cites 'Table 5', but the RxR numbers are in Table 6. Table 6 reports only SR/nDTW/sDTW (no TL/NE/SPL). Many further R2R val-unseen ablation rows exist but are not listed here: per-edit-type with and without back-translation, fixed-style ablation, curriculum learning, number of masked classes, and per-scene results. The adaptive curriculum learning result (57.6 SR) is given only in text. It is not stated whether the HAMT-based runs also use back-translation.
results: On R2R test-unseen, the HAMT + EnvEdit ensemble reaches SR 68.2 / SPL 63.9, versus HAMT's 65/60, a new leaderboard SOTA. The non-pretrained EnvDrop-CLIP + E_is1^m reaches 60.6 / 54.4, beating EnvDrop-CLIP (59/53). On RxR test-unseen, the HAMT ensemble gets nDTW 64.6 / sDTW 51.8 (vs HAMT 59.9 / 45.2), and non-pretrained EnvDrop-CLIP + mBERT + E_st gets 56.4 / 40.4 (vs EnvDrop-CLIP 51.1 / 32.4). Every single edit type improves the reproduced EnvDrop on R2R val-unseen: E_st lifts SR 51.3→56.5 with ViT-B/32 and 55.1→58.2 with ViT-B/16. The best single-model HAMT variant (E_is1^m) reaches 67.9 SR / 62.9 SPL on R2R val-unseen, versus HAMT's 65.7 / 60.9.
limitations: Which edit type is best is inconsistent across visual features and base agents, and combining edited environments during training (curriculum or adaptive curriculum) fails to beat a single edit type; the SOTA leaderboard numbers rely on a 3-model test-time ensemble.

Relies on classic 2019-era style-transfer and SPADE GANs. Style-transferred scenes are artistic and unrealistic, and generation quality limits the gains; the authors note that better image-to-image models could help.

Edits are applied offline per discretized view (precomputed features), with no guarantee of multi-view or 3D consistency across viewpoints. The work is evaluated only on discrete-graph R2R/RxR, not in continuous or real-world settings.
